say: Transforming how we lead together: a handbook for moving from hierarchies towards co-creation.

Public organisations are under enormous pressure. Climate change, A.I., an ageing population, loneliness and burnout. These challenges are complex and connected, and can't be solved inside one department.
Many organisations say they want self-leadership and trust-based leadership. But as one public servant put it: I have never experienced any of that in practice.
This handbook grew out of four years of participatory research with Swedish municipalities and agencies, exploring leadership through choreography, photography, poetry and design.
Its central idea: real change happens on three levels at once. The I, our inner beliefs. The we, our relationships and culture. And the it, our structures and processes.
Six chapters move from why we need to change, through self-leadership, culture and new roles, to participatory structures, and designing your own transformation journey.
Along the way are tried and tested practices, from the core quadrant and dialogue, to consent-based decisions and movement scores for your team.
You'll hear voices from the field, and follow Elena, a fictional manager in elderly care, trying to lead differently inside a system full of barriers.
Here you can search the whole handbook, browse the practice library, time a movement score, and keep a private reflection journal.
Leading together isn't a destination. It's a practice. Start wherever you are. You are not alone.
